The routing module places chunk boundaries by measuring the cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs [1]. It calculates boundary probabilities based on the intuition that consecutive vectors spanning a semantic shift will exhibit lower similarity [1]. Specifically, it projects vectors into a latent space and computes a probability score where low cosine similarity results in a high boundary probability [1]. A boundary is indicated when this probability exceeds a threshold of 0.5 [1]. This process allows the model to dynamically draw chunk boundaries without external supervision [2].

The routing module places chunk boundaries by measuring the cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs [3]. The routing module computes a similarity score between each pair of adjacent encoder outputs by projecting them ( qₜ = W_q x̂ₜ, kₜ₋₁ = W_k x̂ₜ₋₁ ) and taking their cosine similarity; the resulting boundary probability pₜ = 1 − (qₜᵀkₜ₋₁)/(‖qₜ‖‖kₜ₋₁‖) is high when the similarity is low, and a boundary is placed whenever pₜ ≥ 0.5 [1]. This similarity‑based scoring lets the model dynamically draw chunk boundaries at points of semantic shift [3].
